reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir (under renovation) and Nursery Pond fishing report
reports.text:
The 70-acre pond has been stocked by the AGFC with mature bass, crappie, catfish and bream (as well as rainbow trout for the cold weather months).
According to AGFC Fisheries staff, there have definitely been times where it is getting a bunch of use and people are catching bream and smaller bass.

reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were good, with anglers along the shoreline having best success using jigs and worms. Black bass were fair; try a soft plastic worm, or go with a Chatterbait. Two weeks ago, an angler hauled in a bass in the 5- to 6-pound range.

reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
It is stocked with bass, crappie, bream and catfish.
(updated 10-22-2026) This one-time great trophy bass destination when it first opened in the 1990s appears headed back to that designation again, based on what anglers have been catching in the past few months since regulations were eased on bass and crappie. Two bass over 10 pounds were pulled out during the spring, one qualifying for the AGFC’s Legacy Lunker program before the March 31 cutoff. The survey produced bass in the 6-pound range, but AGFC staff continue to track and value reports from local anglers who have documented catches of 8 pounds and larger.

reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bing Watkins at Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) said one angler has caught some nice largemouth bass. Another angler out early in the morning on a boat this week caught a few crappie that were about 11½ inches in length.
“You can see some bass moving around, chasing shad near the shoreline,” Bing said.

reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Brewer Lake is a good getaway in the fall for crappie fishing as well as picking up some decent-sized largemouth bass. For crappie, focus on coves in the northern portion of the lake. Look for bass as temperatures fall around secondary points and isolated brush. Anglers may keep up to 10 largemouths, but only one of those may exceed 16 inches.

reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: As usual we are seeing small pods of bass chasing shad and catching them casting spoons, swimbaits and trolling For the crappie fishermen, the crappie are in fall transition with the water starting to cool. Deeper brushpiles near the channels at the entrance of coves and smaller creek arms are holding some nice crappie.

reports.title: Arkansas’ Lake Ouachita: Where Smart Crappie Fishing Pays Off
reports.text:
Oklahoma crappie pro Todd Huckabee used a detailed game plan to help him
find Lake Ouachita’s clear-water slabs the first time he fished this huge impoundment.
Arkansas’ Lake Ouachita: Where Smart Crappie Fishing Pays Off
Story and photos by Keith Sutton
Some crappie lakes give up their secrets easily. Lake Ouachita isn’t one of them.
That’s not to say the fishing is poor. Quite the opposite. Arkansas’ largest lake has an excellent population of black and white crappie, and anglers who understand how to find them can enjoy some mighty fine fishing.
